FINDING_ID: MM_F001  
SEVERITY: 0.96  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.82  
DESCRIPTION: In Appendix §7.3, the condition “When this inequality holds, dY/dt > 0 despite declining finding rate” is mathematically inconsistent with the stated definition \(Y(t)=N(t)\cdot \bar H(t)\). Differentiating gives \(dY/dt=\lambda(t)\bar H(t)+N(t)\,d\bar H/dt\). Since \(\lambda(t)=dN/dt\ge 0\) for cumulative finding count, \(dY/dt\) does not require the “ascending abstraction” inequality to stay positive; it is already positive whenever either term is nonnegative. The published inequality compares relative depth increase to relative rate decrease, which is relevant to acceleration/quality-shift arguments, not to the sign of \(dY/dt\) under the stated \(Y\).  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace the claim with one of: (a) redefine instantaneous value rate as \(y(t)=\lambda(t)\bar H(t)\), then the inequality can govern whether value rate increases despite declining \(\lambda\); or (b) keep \(Y(t)=N(t)\bar H(t)\) and state only that the inequality characterises “deepening despite declining rate,” not positivity of \(dY/dt\).  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F002  
SEVERITY: 0.93  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.88  
DESCRIPTION: Appendix §7.4 contains a symbol-definition contradiction: it first defines \(k(t)\) as “the local exponential decay rate of the sliding-window generation rate \(v_w(t)\),” then immediately states “\(v_w(t)\) is the sliding-window smoothed generation rate. \(\lambda(t)\) is the empirical decay rate estimated from consecutive round values.” That second sentence reassigns the decay-rate role to \(\lambda(t)\), but in §7.1 \(\lambda(t)\) is the Duane NHPP intensity, not a local decay rate. This is an internal notation conflict.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Keep \(k(t)\) as the local decay-rate symbol and change the sentence to “\(v_w(t)\) is the sliding-window smoothed generation rate. \(\lambda(t)\) is the global Duane NHPP intensity from §7.1.”  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F003  
SEVERITY: 0.90  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.86  
DESCRIPTION: Appendix §6 claims under Reduction Properties that “\(C_M(k)=1-\Pi_{i=1}^{n_M}(1-d_{M,i}p_{M,i,k})\) — machine cumulative detection (= \(F_n\)).” That equality is false as written. \(C_M(k)\) is a per-class detection term; \(F_n\) elsewhere is the weighted sum across classes, \(F_n=\sum_k w_k C_M(k)\). So the appendix conflates a per-class component with the aggregate metric.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Change the parenthetical to “machine cumulative detection for class \(k\) (the per-class term inside \(F_n\))” or define \(F_{n,k}=C_M(k)\) explicitly.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F004  
SEVERITY: 0.88  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.84  
DESCRIPTION: Appendix §6 states the reduction “\(K=1,d=1,\) uniform \(p \Rightarrow C(n)\)” for \(G_n\). This is incomplete/incorrect without also requiring no human stream or appropriate collapse of machine/human passes into one homogeneous stream with \(\rho_{MH}=0\) and identical pass structure. As written, \(G_n\) still contains both machine and human terms, so it does not generally reduce to the simple corroboration model merely from \(K=1,d=1,\) uniform \(p\).  
PROPOSED_FIX: Replace with a properly qualified reduction, e.g. “When there is a single pass stream (either \(n_H=0\) and machine-only, or machine/human streams are collapsed into one independent stream), \(K=1\), \(d=1\), and all pass probabilities equal \(p\), the model reduces to \(C(n)=1-(1-p)^n\).”  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F005  
SEVERITY: 0.86  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.79  
DESCRIPTION: Appendix §1 “Termination-aware \(R_n\)” proposes \(\pi_k(\text{exhausted})=\pi_k+(1-\pi_k)\Delta(k_{\max})\). But \(\Delta(k_{\max})\) was defined in the core directives as a count of revised claims in the terminal pass, not a probability in \([0,1]\). Using it directly in a convex-combination formula is dimensionally inconsistent and can push \(\pi_k\) above 1.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Normalise the terminal revision count before insertion, e.g. \(\hat\Delta=\Delta(k_{\max})/|claim\_set|\), then define \(\pi_k'=\pi_k+(1-\pi_k)\hat\Delta\), or introduce a separate bounded inflation parameter \(r\in[0,1]\) derived from \(\Delta\).  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F006  
SEVERITY: 0.84  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.83  
DESCRIPTION: Appendix §8.2 first presents “Emergence condition: \(Y_{composite}(t)> \max Y_i(t)+k\hat\sigma(Y)\)” and then states that this weaker condition “should not be used alone” because it is satisfiable by trivial aggregation. That is a direct internal inconsistency: the text labels it an emergence condition, then says it is insufficient for genuine emergence.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rename the first condition to “weak emergence screen” or “superiority-over-best-individual condition,” and reserve “strong emergence condition” for \(Y_{composite}(t)>Y_{union}(t)+k\hat\sigma(Y)\).  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F007  
SEVERITY: 0.82  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.64  
DESCRIPTION: Appendix §7.8 describes \(L_{total}\) as a “standard Naive Bayes log-odds update,” but the formula omits prior log-odds. As written, \(S_v=1/(1+e^{-L_{total}})\) implicitly assumes prior odds 1:1. That may be intentional, but the wording is mathematically incomplete and invites misimplementation.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either add the prior term explicitly, \(L_{post}=L_0+L_{total}\), or state that the formulation assumes a neutral prior \(L_0=0\).  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F008  
SEVERITY: 0.79  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.76  
DESCRIPTION: In dynamic_management.py, `ManagerEventType` defines `FORMAT_VIOLATION`, but `FailureHandler.detect_failure()` emits `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED` for format failures instead of `FORMAT_VIOLATION`. This is an implementation discrepancy between the typed failure model and emitted interface events, and it undermines any downstream metric intended to distinguish malformed from merely non-compliant output.  
PROPOSED_FIX: In the FORMAT branch of `detect_failure()`, emit `ManagerEventType.FORMAT_VIOLATION` instead of `ManagerEventType.MALFORMED`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F009  
SEVERITY: 0.76  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.73  
DESCRIPTION: Appendix §2 defines the parser-yield detection condition as \(|raw\_chars(i)|>\tau_{chars}\land \phi_i<\tau_\phi\), where \(\tau_\phi\) is typically 0.5 and \(\phi_i=|F_{parsed}|/|F_{actual}|\). In code, `DetectorHealthMonitor.record_model_round()` triggers the parser-yield diagnosis only when `response_chars > 2000 and finding_count == 0 and not failed`, i.e. effectively \(\phi=0\) only. Partial parser failure (\(0<\phi<\tau_\phi\)) is not implemented.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Pass both parsed and actual/rescued finding counts into the monitor, compute \(\phi_i\), and trigger when \(\phi_i<\tau_\phi\), not only at zero parsed findings.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F010  
SEVERITY: 0.74  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.71  
DESCRIPTION: Appendix §2 states the combined effective detection probability is sequentially \(q_{ik}=f_{del}(i)\cdot \phi_i \cdot d_{ik}\cdot p_{ik}\). The codebase detects analogues of \(f_{del}\) (empty output/failure) and \(\phi_i\) (zero parsed findings with large raw response), but these factors are not propagated into any coverage/detection calculation; they are only used for diagnostics. So the implementation does not realise the stated mathematical extension.  
PROPOSED_FIX: If this appendix is meant to be implemented here, thread delivery and parser yield factors into the effective per-model capability or detection metrics used by convergence/routing; otherwise explicitly note in the appendix or code that these factors are operational diagnostics only, not yet integrated into \(F_n\)-style calculations.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F011  
SEVERITY: 0.71  
FLAW_CLASS: 8  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.67  
DESCRIPTION: The code header claims “No collision with immutable symbols from §7-8 of the existing Mathematical Appendix,” but the file then introduces a `gamma` estimate in `estimate_gamma()` with semantics different from the appendix’s \(\gamma=1-\beta\) convergence parameter. The symbol collision is at least documentary, and likely conceptual, because the code’s estimator formula is not the same object as the appendix’s definition.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Rename the code diagnostic to `gamma_hat_duane` or similar, and update the header comment to avoid the “no collision” claim unless symbol semantics really match.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F012  
SEVERITY: 0.69  
FLAW_CLASS: 5  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.75  
DESCRIPTION: `ConvergenceDetector.estimate_gamma()` is mathematically inconsistent with Appendix §7.1. The appendix defines \(\gamma=1-\beta\) where \(\beta\) is the Duane NHPP shape parameter from \(\lambda(t)=(\beta/\eta)(t/\eta)^{\beta-1}\). The code instead computes `log(round_idx) / (log(cum_r) - log(cum_1))`, which is not \(1-\beta\) and is not documented as a valid estimator for that parameter. This is a model/code discrepancy.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either implement an estimator derived from fitting the Duane model and then setting \(\hat\gamma=1-\hat\beta\), or rename the function to avoid claiming it estimates the appendix’s \(\gamma\).  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F013  
SEVERITY: 0.63  
FLAW_CLASS: 4  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.58  
DESCRIPTION: Appendix §7.5 defines \(O_A\) using “verified findings in \(F_{conv}\)” with a non-verifiable-domain guard requiring at least 2 verifiable findings. The code contains no implementation of \(O_A\), \(S_{sync}\), \(M_{suppress}\), or \(\Delta_{adopt}/\Delta_{drop}\) despite operational comments elsewhere referring to adoption stabilisation. The mathematical appendix and implementation status are therefore only partially aligned.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Either implement these metrics in the management layer where convergence is assessed, or narrow the appendix/code cross-reference by documenting that §7.5–§7.6 are not yet implemented in `dynamic_management.py`.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

FINDING_ID: MM_F014  
SEVERITY: 0.58  
FLAW_CLASS: 3  
ABSTRACTION_INDEX: 0.49  
DESCRIPTION: Appendix notation around \(\Delta\) is inconsistent across §7.5, §7.6, and the Notation Summary. §7.5 says “\(\bar\Delta\) is the mean Adoption Delta across all model pairs,” while §7.6 defines \(\bar\Delta(A\to B)\) as a directional pairwise scalar. Those are different objects but share the same symbol.  
PROPOSED_FIX: Use distinct notation, e.g. \(\bar\Delta_{pair}(A\to B)\) for pairwise and \(\bar\Delta_{global}\) for mean across pairs.  
VERIFIED: TRUE

Definitive stance: the appendix is not internally clean enough to call fully mathematically consistent, and the code only partially implements the stated model extensions. The highest-confidence issues are the incorrect derivative claim in §7.3, notation collision in §7.4, per-class/aggregate conflation in §6, and the model/code mismatches around gamma estimation, parser-yield handling, and format-failure event typing.
